title: Yami no Majo
type: Venerable Rahu mage and cultural intermediary
dek: A respected mage who explains what Rahu membership permits—and whose quiet fan gestures reveal the labor beneath Rahu refinement.

facts.Access rule: Membership permits learning and use; outsider teaching prohibited

sources: Yami_no_Majo_NPC_Master.md — supplied 5 October 2026; consolidated NPC history with evidence and visibility distinctions
body:
Yami no Majo is a respected Rahu spellcaster introduced by Samurai Osu as a venerable mage. Her principal recovered scene is a conference on 20 August 2024 with adventurers seeking to understand or join the Rahu. She answers questions about magical knowledge, initiation, and the customs that make Rahu society work.

The surviving record supports a senior and trusted magical figure. It does not establish her age, species, spell list, class level, noble rank, or membership in the Witch Queen’s inner council. Her name is preserved without inventing a formal translation or treating “no Majo” as a separately established office.

20 August 2024: the conference

Samurai Osu brings Yami and Shogun Yoshida to meet the visiting adventurers. Yoshida is identified as a lead architect despite the joking Shogun title; Yami is introduced for her magical expertise. She bows, and the visitors return the courtesy.

Eugene is especially interested in contamination, the Warping Lattice or delirium, and methods that could help people beyond Rahu territory. Yami takes his questions seriously. Her role is to explain access and obligation; the scene does not disclose the mechanics of a secret anti-contamination technique.

“For you would be one of us”

Asked whether restricted tactics would become available if Eugene proved worthy and became Rahu, Yami answers:

But of course, for you would be one of us.Yami no Majo

The boundary can change through membership. At least some outsiders can become Rahu, and learning is tied to the obligations they accept. Yami is a teacher before that threshold; she does not independently pronounce an outsider initiated during this conversation. Witch Queen Ephraith and the wider institution hold the authority to determine membership.

When Eugene asks whether he could use the methods elsewhere to help people, Yami permits use while retaining a strict limit:

Of course, though teaching others would be strictly prohibited.Yami no Majo

Learning a method does not give the individual unlimited authority to pass it on. Her explanation treats specialist knowledge as a collective trust. Eugene later suspects that initiation may involve a geas; that is his theory, not a mechanism Yami confirms here.

The etiquette of unseen service

When Empty directly asks a Dasa for food, Yami stops him and says the request should go through her. She explains that the Dasa work to remain unseen and anticipate needs; calling attention to them exposes a failure in that ideal of service.

Olokun recognizes the fan-signaling custom, and Yami demonstrates it. A stroke and tilt of her fan sends the Dasa for spicy stew, ghost peppers, thin venison slices, vegetable broth, and coffee without a spoken order.

Her stated explanation presents this as proper etiquette. The same observed behavior shows how elite comfort depends on labor whose visibility is deliberately minimized. That interpretation can coexist with the custom she describes without inventing a confession of cruelty or assuming she privately rejects the system.

What others say after she leaves

After Yami departs, Lucido reports that Rahu architectural plans suggest Dasa life-force contributes to construction. The adventurers discuss exploitation and possible magical enforcement of caste.

Those are Lucido’s reported discovery and the outsiders’ interpretations, not statements Yami makes. Her direct scene establishes Dasa service, anticipation, fan signals, and her explanation of dishonor. It does not establish that she personally uses Dasa life-force, knows the full mechanism, or confessed such a practice.

A signal calls her away

Another fan movement catches Yami’s attention. She looks startled, apologizes that her services are needed, and leaves. The signaling system can direct someone of her standing as well as the people serving the room.

Her status therefore carries obligations too. The record does not identify who summoned her or why. Nor does it supply a complete fan alphabet or make every possible signal canonical.

People and institutions around her

  • Witch Queen Ephraith: the sovereign connected to the initiation process. Yami’s exact private relationship with her remains unknown.
  • Samurai Osu: the official who brings and introduces her as a respected specialist.
  • Shogun Yoshida: the architect introduced alongside her; their deeper relationship is not recovered.
  • Eugene: a serious seeker of knowledge who later expresses attraction to her. No recovered response establishes that Yami reciprocates it.
  • Empty and the Dasa: participants in the exchange that exposes the logic of elite service.
  • Olokun: a visitor already learning fan etiquette and part of the conference.
  • Lucido Spettoro: the source of later architectural claims, whose account remains distinct from Yami’s.

The open record

Her personal history, magical specialization, exact authority, understanding of the Dasa system, the full fan language, subsequent meetings with Eugene, and fate during the Rahu war remain unresolved. Her importance rests on what this one substantial scene reveals about knowledge, belonging, and the obligations surrounding privilege.
